relevance_note: The paper describes 17 children with paediatric-onset HA20 and several of their affected relatives one by one and states 'All patients carried a pathogenic or likely pathogenic TNFAIP3 variant.'
method_note: Read only the paper, schema_ha20_v5.json and extraction_rules_v1.md; no script could be run, so every row was transcribed by hand and every span re-checked character for character against the Markdown. LABELS: 'P1'-'P17' is the paper's own per-patient label (column headers of supplementary tables 1a-1c); the running text also writes 'patient 7' and table 3 'Patient 4'. is_proband is false with span null for everyone, because the words proband and index case never appear. SPANS for the two patient-as-column tables (supplementary tables 1a and 1b) are the table row quoted from its row label through that patient's cell, that is, the cumulative prefix of the row, which is contiguous and verbatim in the paper; the column header is named in the method note here: in supplementary table 1a the data columns are P1 to P17 from left to right, and in supplementary table 1b likewise. VARIANT FIELDS: table 3 prints one row per patient, so P1-P3 (c. 547C>T) and P10-P13 (c. 971_975del) each get their own row with the same printed variant and P4, P7 and P8 share c. 259C>T. variant_type 'nonsense' is given only for the three variants the paper itself calls stop-gain variants; 'Most of our patients (58 %) harboured OTU nonsense/frameshift mutations' is a cohort-level list of two classes and was applied to nobody, so the other variants are 'not reported' even though the paper says 'only one missense variant was identified'. zygosity is 'not reported' everywhere: the paper states autosomal dominant inheritance and haploinsufficiency but never says heterozygous for any person, so rule 8's monoallelic wording was not applied. inheritance 'inherited unspecified parent' only for P17, the one patient with a stated carrier parent. The ACMG statement (PVS1 + PM2, 9 points) is recorded only for P6 and P14, the patients named in the sentence that carries it, although that sentence may describe the paper's mutations in general. The p. Pro457Alafs*16 sentence is a prediction, not an assay. No variant row was created for the affected relatives of families 2 and 8: the paper ties the family variant to them only through the general statement that relatives carry identical mutations, never per person; the parent of P17 is the one relative stated to carry 'the same variant', so that row exists with variant_original_string 'not reported'. source_reference_in_review copies the table 3 Reference(s) cell for every patient. RELATIVES: 11 are included (family 2: mother, grandfather, aunt, two nieces and cousin of P4; family 8: half-brother, half-sister, mother and maternal grandfather of P10; family 12: the parent of P17). The aunt and two nieces are given as relatives of P4's grandfather and the cousin's relation is unspecified ('another cousin'), so those labels chain to the grandfather: an interpretation. Supplementary figures 1 (pedigrees) and 2 (timelines) are converted with a scrambled layout and no patient labels, so no fact was taken from them. INCONSISTENCIES FOUND: (1) the text says P7 received baricitinib 'with partial clinical improvement' while supplementary table 1c prints effectiveness 'no' for P7; (2) the text reports 'mildly elevated faecal calprotectin' for P1 while table 1b prints 'neg'; (3) positive ANA is given as 7/13 in the text but 8 of the 14 printed cells are '+'; (4) hypergammaglobulinaemia '4/11' in the text vs 3 printed 'yes'; (5) elevated IgA '3/11' vs 4 printed 'yes'; (6) median age at diagnosis 13.5 years (table 1) vs 13 years (text). PHENOTYPES: for supplementary table 1a the onset block and the disease-course block were merged into one status per feature (observed if Present in either block, excluded only if Absent in both) and the supporting row is the one quoted, so the timing is not recorded per row; my transcription reproduces all 22 N (%) values printed in table 2. 'Absent' and 'Present' are self-defining words; the table 1b legend ('Yes/No, presence / absence of the feature; +/-, positive/negative results; /, data not available; neg, normal or negative result') was used for the ANA/FR/dsDNA cells; the '0' printed for dsDNA in P7 and the '1' printed for IgM in P15 are not covered by that legend and were treated as not reported. Judgements I made: 'Fever' mapped to checklist 'recurrent fever'; 'Skin eruption' to 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)'; P10's 'autoimmune diabetes' to 'type 1 diabetes'; colitis, P1's aphthoid colonic ulcerations and P8's gastritis to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; the paper's neurological symptom (headache) to 'central nervous system involvement'; for relatives described only with 'ulcers' the checklist item 'oral ulcers' was used. Presence of one component was taken as 'observed' for a composite item, but an explicitly absent single component was not used to exclude a composite (lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy; pericarditis or other serositis), except that the cohort-level statements naming the positive patients ('Ocular involvement occurred in one patient (5.9%, patient 12)'; 'two patients (patient 1 and 8, 11.8%) had autoimmune thyroiditis'; 'One patient (patient 10, 5.9%) had autoimmune diabetes'; 'two patients (patients 6 and 8, 11.8%) had autoimmune hepatitis'; 'Neurological symptoms were noted in three patients (17.6%)') were used to mark the other patients 'excluded' with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' is 'not reported' for everyone: the tables print only numbers with no per-person reference range and the only 'elevated' statement is cohort-level. 'cytopenia (autoimmune)', 'recurrent infections' (despite P16's recurrent pharyngotonsillitis, recorded as its own feature), 'growth failure', 'interstitial lung disease' and 'vasculitis' are 'not reported' for everyone. 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' is observed where a printed antibody cell is positive or the text names one (P7 anti-TPO antibodies, P8 gastric autoantibodies), and excluded only for P15, whose ANA, FR and dsDNA cells are all '-'. HPO candidates are null because no identifier could be verified from the allowed sources. No stacked ' / ' cell was used for any person: they occur only in the flare rows of supplementary table 1a and in supplementary table 2, a disease-comparison table with no patients. Age ISO values keep the printed decimals (P0.3Y for '0.3'). Ethnicity, vital status and age at last evaluation are not reported per person: the paper gives them only as cohort figures, and the figure-caption ages (14 and 15 years) are ages at imaging. treatment_summary lists the drugs the paper reports for that patient; spans are capped at five, so a long regimen is not quoted in full.
